answer: Ephemeral harbor attestations. Each identity must collect signed attestations from a random rotating panel of peers before acting; attestations expire after one voyage cycle. Panels are drawn from long-lived accounts whose history is publicly auditable, so a clone farm must first cultivate aged, non-suspicious accounts. Every new identity pays an issuance fee plus the labor of acquiring fresh attestations each cycle. Because the vine of trust resets, holding many clones costs recurring attestation work and fees, while a single honest identity pays once.
